item.research_question: What are the individual effects of Mo, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr on the microstructure and mechanical properties (yield strength, ductility, and elevated-temperature performance) of equiatomic Hf-Mo-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr refractory high-entropy alloys?
item.material_system: Equiatomic HfMoNbTaTiZr and its five sub-alloys created by the subtraction method: HfNbTaTiZr, HfMoTaTiZr, HfMoNbTiZr, HfMoNbTaZr, and HfMoNbTaTi
item.processing_route: Vacuum-arc melting of 99.9 wt.% (99.99 wt.% for Ti) pure elements stacked by melting point, re-melted at least four times, and solidified in a water-cool copper mold
item.test_conditions: Compression tests at room temperature, 800 °C, 1000 °C, 1200 °C, and 1400 °C; crosshead speed 0.36 mm/min (strain rate 10⁻³ s⁻¹); cylindrical samples 3.6 mm diameter x 6 mm height
key_findings: HfMoNbTaTiZr alloy yield strength was 1512 MPa at room temperature and 556 MPa at 1200 °C.
HfMoTaTiZr (Nb removed) showed the highest room temperature yield strength of 1600 MPa but lower toughness.
HfMoNbTaTi (Zr removed) exhibited the best comprehensive properties with 27% fracture strain at room temperature and 367 MPa yield strength at 1400 °C.
The presence of Mo increased room temperature yield strength from 929 MPa (in HfNbTaTiZr) to 1512 MPa but reduced fracture strain from >50% to 12%.
Nb addition increased yield strength by 38% at 1200 °C and significantly improved room temperature fracture strain.
Zr addition increased strength but strongly deteriorated room temperature toughness, reducing fracture strain from 27% to 12%.
Alloys with Mo present showed much better strength at elevated temperatures compared to HfNbTaTiZr.
At 1200 °C, HfMoNbTaTi alloy had the highest specific strength among the tested alloys.
item.mechanism: The high yield strength is attributed to the solid solution strengthening effect driven by atomic size and shear modulus mismatch; the high entropy effect promotes the formation of a single BCC disordered solid solution phase despite binary phase diagrams suggesting intermetallics; severe lattice distortion reduces the effective shear modulus by approximately 30% compared to the rule of mixtures.
item.limitations: There is a deviation of about 30% between calculated and experimental yield strengths, likely due to overestimated shear modulus; the criteria for Laves phase formation were not fully consistent with experimental observations; the reduction in shear modulus due to lattice distortion requires further research to confirm reasons.
item.future_work: Further modification of composition and/or anti-oxidation coatings are required for high-temperature applications in air; more research is needed to confirm the elemental effects in other RHEA systems and to understand the reasons for reduced shear modulus.
quotes: The subtraction method was applied on equiatomic HfMoNbTaTiZr alloys to discover the role of each element
HfMoNbTaTi has the best mechanical performance, that is, 27% compressive strain at room temperature and yield strength 367 MPa at 1400 °C
The high entropy effect of the present alloys is significant in enhancing the formation of a solid solution
